[After years of planning](https://voat.co/v/ModernPowers/comments/985173), ground is finally being broken on a new major overseas base to replace US assets being given up on including Guantanamo Bay and various Middle Eastern outposts. The new base, [located in northern Mauritania](http://www.scribblemaps.com/maps/view/joint_base/75XC9K5WJV), will serve both nations' militaries, providing an important naval and air force logistical hub for US operations in Africa.

Construction of the Air Base is expected to cost about $2 billion ([m] [figure from the Qatari base built for the US - $1b original construction, $.5b later upgrades, $.5b inflation](http://www.thenation.com/article/base-america/)) while the naval base portion is expected to cost about $1 billion ([m] [figure from the US-South Korean Jeju base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeju_Naval_Base)). The base is expected to be complete by 2025.

Funding for the base will be paid for by [existing US military funding for new construction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_budget_of_the_United_States#By_title) that no longer needs to be spent on the clandestine Middle Eastern bases.
